trust_decision.summary: Every HTTP fetch of a caller-supplied URL must validate each redirect hop's target (scheme + resolved IP) before following it; decided centrally in crewai_tools.security.safe_requests.safe_get and applied at every requests.get call site that fetches a user/LLM-supplied URL.

landing_point.why: The summary says the scrape tools' SSRF check is bypassed by a redirect; this is the canonical validate_url-then-requests.get pattern, and the tool's own docstring advertises URL scraping.

fix_sites.entry_point: load_from_url, used by JSONLoader, XMLLoader, CSVLoader, MDXLoader (all via RagTool)
safe_get, imported by all seven call sites above

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The RAG loader layer ingests document sources, not free-form agent-supplied URLs, and load_from_url is a generic helper buried in rag/ while the advisory reads as being about the scraping tools; fixing the two scrapers is 'the fix'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects must keep Authorization/Cookie headers and the cookies dict (authenticated scraping), and ordinary 301/302 hops (http->https, trailing slash, www) must still be followed; a fix that refuses all redirects or strips all credentials breaks these paths.

O6_input_shapes: initial http(s) URL whose hostname resolves to a private/reserved IP
absolute Location redirect to an internal address (301/302/303/307/308)
relative Location redirect resolved against the current URL with urljoin
cross-origin redirect that must drop Authorization/Cookie/x-api-key/token headers and cookies
redirect chain longer than max_redirects (must fail closed)
Location with a non-http scheme (file://) which validate_url must reject

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Skill download fetches a registry-supplied download_url with httpx and follow_redirects=True, with no URL validation at all before the request
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It lives in the core crewai package and the experimental skills feature, and the URL comes from the trusted crewai registry API response rather than from the model or a tool argument.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CrewDoclingSource validates only URL shape (scheme, netloc, a dot in the host) and then hands the URL to docling's converter, which performs the fetch and follows redirects
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: third-party docling does the actual fetch, and this is the core knowledge-source path rather than a crewai-tools scraper.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: JinaScrapeWebsiteTool validates the user URL, then requests https://r.jina.ai/{url} with redirects enabled, so any Location the reader endpoint returns is followed unvalidated
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the request target is the fixed public r.jina.ai host and the user URL is only a path segment, so it 'cannot' reach internal services.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Serply news search follows each result link with requests.get (redirects on) without any validate_url call; the fetched URLs come from the search API response
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the links are produced by a third-party search API, not supplied by the caller, and the tool only reads r.history to report the final link.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Provider-backed tools validate the URL and then POST it to the provider (BrightData, Serper, Scrapfly, Firecrawl, Hyperbrowser), which fetches it and handles redirects server-side
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the fetch happens on the provider's infrastructure, so local redirect validation is irrelevant and the initial-URL check is all that is owed.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling tool directory, same package (five tools share the shape)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third scraping tool that fetches the caller URL directly with requests.get instead of delegating to a provider SDK
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it already calls validate_url(url) and then starts a scrape job with that URL, exactly the shape of the two fixed tools, so a maintainer could easily have written the direct-fetch variant here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A utilities/safe_requests.py backward-compatible re-export shim alongside the existing safe_path shim
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project keeps old crewai_tools.utilities.* import paths alive for the security helpers, so a sibling helper would be expected to get the same shim and the same redirect logic.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A loader in the same package that gates the URL with its own https://github.com/ prefix check instead of validate_url, plus a direct fetch of URLs it derives
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: data_types.py already routes URLs with 'github.com' in the netloc to this loader, and it checks only the prefix before deriving repo and file paths, so adding a plain requests.get for a derived download URL is a natural maintainer step.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A load_from_url sibling for POST/HEAD or for a per-loader timeout, duplicating the redirect walk
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: load_from_url is the shared entry for four loaders and takes an arbitrary accept_header/loader_name, so a second helper for a different verb is a small step for a maintainer.

O9_family: ssrf (CWE-918): URL fetched without validating each redirect target

O10_build.toolchain: uv workspace / pyproject.toml (lib/crewai-tools/pyproject.toml), pytest with monkeypatch-based HTTP mocking and a few VCR cassettes
O10_build.project_tests: lib/crewai-tools/tests/rag/test_webpage_loader.py, tests/rag/test_json_loader.py, tests/rag/test_mdx_loader.py, tests/rag/test_docx_loader.py and tests/utilities/test_safe_path.py exist at the pinned commit; the fix adds tests/rag/conftest.py and tests/utilities/test_safe_requests.py (both new files) that mock requests.get and socket.getaddrinfo, so the fixed behaviour is testable offline.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add allow_redirects=False to the two scrapers' requests.get calls (or re-run validate_url once on the response URL), which hands 3xx bodies to callers and leaves every RAG loader untouched.
